original_test_intent: Verify the installed CPU is recognized and its defined frequency behavior matches the approved processor specification under controlled BIOS, governor, power, load and thermal conditions.
original_method: Operator installs CPU/cooling, powers on and captures BIOS/Windows/Linux recognition; after stable boot, agent securely collects full CPU identity, governor/min/max/base data and timestamped per-CPU frequency samples under the approved condition; engineer judges the selected frequency definition.
manual_activity: Operator installs CPU/cooling, powers on and captures BIOS/Windows recognition; engineering defines frequency criterion before secure Linux sampling.
required_inputs: Approved CPU/board/BIOS/cooling identity and qualified operator
Clarification that frequency, not core count, is authoritative and exact base/nominal/turbo/sustained criterion
Expected per-model frequency values/tolerance and approved idle/load sampling condition
Linux governor/min/max/boost/power/thermal profile plus Windows coverage if mandatory
Secure access, sampling duration/cadence and thermal/SEL abort/recovery policy
safety_requirements: Use qualified ESD/cooling/power handling for installation
Do not change governor, BIOS power limits, boost/overclock or thermal settings without approval
Use managed authentication and host verification
Stop on thermal/SEL/boot instability, missing CPUs or anomalous frequency behavior
No automatic reboot, profile change or retry
agent_execution_scope: Collect raw CPU identity/topology, cpufreq/sysfs/governor and per-CPU time samples after approval
Relate observations to supplied criterion without issuing verdict
Do not perform installation/BIOS/Windows actions, modify power controls or infer missing frequency definition
engineer_actions: Define frequency type, load state, range/tolerance and required OS coverage
Approve safe sampling profile and review evidence/verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Insufficient and unsafe: first MHz line is instantaneous, grep drops context, and sshpass/host-key bypass are prohibited; it also ignores manual steps and source ambiguity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After criterion approval, securely preserve full `lscpu`, `/proc/cpuinfo`, cpufreq/sysfs governor/min/max/boost data and timestamped per-CPU samples under defined condition.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Frequency item, manual install/Windows/Linux coverage and5/0 planning fields are retained; no fabricated sampling duration is treated as Master authority.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind CPU identity, BIOS/power/governor/load/thermal state and per-CPU samples to a versioned frequency criterion.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds dynamic measurement context, secure access, measurable acceptance and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Core count or one instantaneous MHz value cannot establish frequency compliance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Frequency changes with P-state, boost, load, governor, power limits, thermal headroom and virtualization.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must state whether Windows and Linux are both mandatory and which frequency definition is authoritative; review cannot infer it from model name.
expected_evidence: Timestamped per-CPU samples with defined load/idle condition
Thermal/power, dmesg/syslog/SEL and final stable state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and first sentence target frequency, but step3 says core number and Criteria only address installation/generic CPU information. No frequency definition or acceptance exists.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Engineering can resolve the criterion and provide hardware/operator/access; the case remains reviewable and executable afterward.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row19 Wistron-Processor-00002-V003: confirm Frequency is authoritative instead of the copied core-number step/generic Criteria; define base, nominal, turbo or sustained frequency, required Windows/Linux and BIOS coverage, idle/load condition, per-CPU sampling duration/cadence, expected range/tolerance, governor/boost/power/thermal profile, approved CPU/board/BIOS/cooling setup, secure access, abort/recovery and invalid-run policy.

review_improvement: Turns an ambiguous instantaneous-reading check into a traceable dynamic-frequency review while retaining manual hardware and OS coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: CPU MHz is not a fixed inventory value: P-states, governor, boost, load and thermal limits move it continuously. A first `/proc/cpuinfo` line can differ across cores and moments and cannot prove base or sustained performance. The source must identify the intended frequency regime before evidence can be interpreted.
